Stalemate happens when the player to move has no legal move and is not in check, for example a black king on h8 against a white king on f7 and a white queen on g6 with Black to move. The game is drawn by the rules of chess because the side to move cannot move, yet the king is not attacked, so it is not checkmate. It stops a player with a big material lead from winning without actually delivering mate, which is why careful technique matters in endgames.
